title: Verify the database and its data / Recoverable S3 versions
summary: Inspect the supplied evidence and distinguish what each check establishes.

steps.title: Verify the database and its data

blocks.text: Instance inspection and the application-data check answer different questions.
Inspect an RDS DB instance’s identifier, engine, endpoint and operational status in the console or with describe-db-instances.
Before the supplied connection attempt, inspect the intended DB instance and check its engine and status.
Use the supplied endpoint, database client and approved credentials to connect. Check the data marker with the supplied query; instance status alone does not verify application data.

nodes.label: Intended RDS instance: identifier, engine, endpoint and status inspected

Observed query outcome: required data marker missing

Intended RDS instance: identifier, engine, endpoint and status inspected → supplied query on intended instance → Observed query outcome: required data marker missing; Expected query outcome: required data marker present → Compare the same marker → Observed query outcome: required data marker missing; Observed query outcome: required data marker missing → missing marker → Acceptable instance status does not establish application-data success.

steps.title: Work through the evidence: Verify the database and its data

blocks.text: Tie the supplied instance identifier and endpoint to the engine/status inspection. Then read the supplied connection and query outcome for the expected data marker. Acceptable status with a missing marker is not a successful data check. Keep the safe query result with the instance context.
Instance status cannot substitute for the data marker, and the marker does not substitute for checking the intended instance.

steps.title: Check verify the database and its data
steps.lede: Read the supplied evidence in this step and choose the interpretation it supports.

public.prompt: The intended RDS instance meets the supplied engine and status requirements. What still verifies application data?

options.text: Connect with the supplied endpoint, client and approved credentials, then compare the supplied query result with the expected data marker.
Treat the operational status as proof that the expected marker exists.
Check the status again and omit the query.

o1.message: This follows the stated evidence and the taught verification rule.

o2.message: Instance status does not verify application data.

o3.message: Repeated status inspection still does not compare the data marker.

correct.message: Your choice follows the stated evidence and verification rule.

incorrect.message: Recheck the evidence and the explanation for the selected option.

hints: Separate the instance check from the application-data check.

steps.title: Review verify the database and its data
steps.lede: Read the supplied excerpts in this step and decide which are correct, defective or unsafe.

public.prompt: Read each RDS verification record and decide whether it verifies both the intended instance and the supplied data marker separately.

buckets.label: Meets the stated criterion / conclusion supported
Does not meet the criterion / conclusion unsupported

items.text:
Identifier equals intended instance. Engine and status equal supplied requirements; endpoint recorded. Connection uses that endpoint, supplied client and approved credentials. Supplied query result equals the expected marker.
Report: instance requirement met; data-marker check met.

Identifier, engine, status and endpoint verified against the intended instance. No connection or query attempted.
Report: instance requirement met; application marker verified by status.

Engine and status meet requirements, but recorded identifier differs from the intended instance. Query against that other instance matches the expected marker.
Report: intended instance and its data verified.

i1.message: Instance identity, requirements and endpoint are recorded, and the query comparison independently verifies the marker.

i2.message: Instance status alone cannot verify the application marker.

i3.message: The query result for another instance does not verify the intended instance.

correct.message: Each judgement follows the supplied excerpt and the verification criterion.

incorrect.message: Check the evidence behind each conclusion; a partial success does not establish every required boundary.

hints: Do not substitute operational status for the query comparison.

blocks.text: Choose the recovery method for the actual overwrite or simple-deletion case.
S3 versioning retains multiple object versions, including versions displaced by an overwrite.
In a versioning-enabled bucket, a simple delete ordinarily adds a delete marker rather than removing earlier versions. Deleting a specified version removes it permanently.
For an overwrite, copy the selected prior version to the same key, creating a new current version. Undo a simple deletion by removing its delete marker to expose the preceding version.
Check noncurrent-version expiration and other lifecycle rules against the required recovery window so needed recoverable versions remain available.

steps.title: Work through the evidence: Recoverable S3 versions

blocks.text: For overwritten releases/orders.zip, copy the required prior version to the same key to create a new current version. For a separate simple deletion, remove the delete marker to expose the preceding version. Check lifecycle expiration against the required recovery window; do not permanently delete a needed specified version.
A simple delete ordinarily creates a marker; a specified-version deletion is permanent. Versioning alone does not guarantee indefinite retention under lifecycle rules.

steps.title: Check recoverable S3 versions
steps.lede: Read the supplied evidence in this step and choose the interpretation it supports.

public.prompt: In a versioning-enabled bucket, an overwrite displaced the wanted version of releases/orders.zip. How is that selected prior version restored as current?

options.text: Remove a delete marker even though this case is an overwrite with no delete marker.
Copy the selected prior version to the same key, creating a new current version.
Permanently delete the selected prior version.

o1.message: Delete-marker removal undoes a simple deletion; this overwrite requires copying the selected prior version.

o2.message: This follows the stated evidence and the taught verification rule.

o3.message: Deleting the desired version removes it rather than restoring its content.

correct.message: Your choice follows the stated evidence and verification rule.

incorrect.message: Recheck the evidence and the explanation for the selected option.

hints: Distinguish restoring an overwrite from undoing a simple delete.

steps.title: Check recoverable S3 versions
steps.lede: Read the supplied evidence in this step and choose the interpretation it supports.

public.prompt: A simple delete created a delete marker for releases/orders.zip in a versioning-enabled bucket; prior versions remain. How is the preceding version exposed again?

options.text: Delete the preceding version by its version ID.
Conclude that the simple delete permanently removed every prior version.

o1.message: This follows the stated evidence and the taught verification rule.

o2.message: Deleting a specified version permanently removes the version needed for recovery.

o3.message: The described simple delete created a marker, not permanent removal of the prior versions.

correct.message: Your choice follows the stated evidence and verification rule.

incorrect.message: Recheck the evidence and the explanation for the selected option.

hints: Identify what now hides the preceding version.

steps.title: Review recoverable S3 versions
steps.lede: Read the supplied excerpts in this step and decide which are correct, defective or unsafe.

public.prompt: Read each bucket protection record and decide whether it establishes the supplied recovery window for releases/orders.zip.

buckets.label: Meets the stated criterion / conclusion supported
Does not meet the criterion / conclusion unsupported

items.text:
Bucket: versioning Enabled. Supplied lifecycle policy applied. Inspection: noncurrent-version expiration and all other applicable rules leave required versions recoverable for the supplied recovery window.
Conclusion: recovery-window requirement met.

Bucket: versioning Enabled. Supplied lifecycle policy applied. Inspection: noncurrent-version expiration removes required versions before the supplied recovery window ends.
Conclusion: recovery-window requirement met because versioning is enabled.

Bucket: versioning Enabled. Lifecycle policy applied; neither noncurrent-version expiration nor other applicable rules inspected.
Conclusion: required recovery window verified.

i1.message: The record establishes both enabled versioning and lifecycle preservation of required versions.

i2.message: Enabled versioning does not override lifecycle removal before the required window.

i3.message: Applying a policy without inspecting applicable expiration rules does not establish recoverability for the window.

correct.message: Each judgement follows the supplied excerpt and the verification criterion.

incorrect.message: Check the evidence behind each conclusion; a partial success does not establish every required boundary.

hints: Check the lifecycle window as well as the versioning setting.

blocks.text: Check the intended instance’s engine and status, then verify its data marker through the supplied connection and query.
Overwrite recovery and delete-marker recovery differ. Check lifecycle rules against the required recoverability window.
